record.paper_title: On an Open Question in Recovering Sturm--Liouville-Type Operators with Delay
record.context_brief: Classification of uniqueness ranges and boundary conditions
record.original_question: Consider the delayed Sturm-Liouville inverse spectral problem in which, for j=0,1, L_j(a,q) is defined by -y''(x)+q(x)y(x-a)=lambda y(x) on 0<x<pi with boundary conditions y(0)=y^(j)(pi)=0, where q is a complex-valued L2(0,pi) potential satisfying q(x)=0 on (0,a), and a is in (0,pi). Given the two spectra {lambda_{n,0}} and {lambda_{n,1}}, for which ranges of the delay parameter a and for which admissible boundary-condition types does this data uniquely determine q, and for which choices does uniqueness fail?

evidence.quote: For $j=0,1,$ denote by $\{\lambda_{n,j}\}$ the spectrum of the boundary value problem ${\cal L}_j(a,q)$ of the form $-y''(x)+q(x)y(x-a)=\lambda y(x),\quad 0<x<\pi,$ $y(0)=y^{(j)}(\pi)=0,$ where $q(x)$ is a complex-valued function in $L_2(0,\pi)$ and $q(x)=0$ on $(0,a),$ while $a\in(0,\pi).$
{\bf Inverse Problem 1.} Given the spectra $\{\lambda_{n,0}\}$ and $\{\lambda_{n,1}\},$ find the potential $q(x).$

Theorem~1 opens the analogous type of questions for Inverse Problem~1, which consist in giving description of ranges of the delay parameter $a$ along with the types of boundary conditions, for which the uniqueness of solution of Inverse Problem~1 takes place.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
For a complex-valued potential $q\in L_2(0,\pi)$ that vanishes on $(0,a)$ where $a\in(0,\pi)$, and for $j=0,1$, let $\mathcal{L}_j(a,q)$ denote the boundary value problem
$$-y''(x)+q(x)\,y(x-a)=\lambda\,y(x),\qquad 0<x<\pi,$$
with the boundary conditions $y(0)=0$ and $y^{(j)}(\pi)=0$ (Dirichlet at $\pi$ for $j=0$, Neumann at $\pi$ for $j=1$). Let $\{\lambda_{n,j}\}_{n\ge 1}$ be the eigenvalue sequence of $\mathcal{L}_j(a,q)$. 

Inverse Problem. Given the two spectra $\{\lambda_{n,0}\}$ and $\{\lambda_{n,1}\}$, recover $q$.

Determine, more generally, the complete classification of pairs $(a,\text{boundary-condition type})$ — where the boundary condition at $0$ and at $\pi$ are each chosen from an admissible family of separated linear conditions — for which the two spectra uniquely determine the potential $q$, and the pairs for which uniqueness fails (i.e., for which there exist iso-bispectral potentials).
artifact.category_tag: Inverse spectral problems for delay Sturm–Liouville operators
artifact.status_search_result: The classification has been advanced but remains incomplete. Uniqueness from the two spectra is known to hold for delays $a\in[2\pi/5,\pi)$ (with Dirichlet/Neumann at $\pi$), while non-uniqueness has been established for $a\in[\pi/3,2\pi/5)$ via explicit families of iso-bispectral potentials. Subsequent works extend results to Robin boundary conditions, graphs with global delay, and small-delay non-uniqueness, but a full classification across all delays $a\in(0,\pi)$ and all admissible boundary-condition types is not yet complete.

status_evidence.title: Iso-bispectral potentials for Sturm-Liouville-type operators with small delay
status_evidence.snippet: Constructs infinite families of iso-bispectral potentials for delays in [pi/3, 2pi/5), giving negative answer to uniqueness in this range.
status_evidence.claim: Non-uniqueness established for a range of small delays.

status_evidence.title: On non-uniqueness of recovering Sturm-Liouville operators with delay and the Neumann boundary condition at zero
status_evidence.snippet: Provides non-uniqueness results for delay operators with certain boundary conditions.

status_evidence.title: On recovering Sturm--Liouville-type operators with global delay on graphs from two spectra
status_evidence.snippet: Extends two-spectra uniqueness results to star graphs with Robin boundary conditions.
status_evidence.claim: Continued partial progress on the classification.

status_evidence.title: Inverse Spectral Problems for Sturm–Liouville Operators with a Constant Delay Less than Half the Length of the Interval and Robin Boundary Conditions
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the regime a < pi/2 with Robin conditions, addressing further cases of the classification.
status_evidence.claim: Partial uniqueness results for delays below pi/2.
